title: Fourier granularity from decision-tree depth
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $T$ be a decision tree on the $n$-coordinate binary cube with real outputs, and let $f$ be an integer-valued function on that cube. If $T$ computes the real-valued function obtained from $f$, then every Fourier coefficient of the corresponding function on the sign cube is an integer multiple of $2^{-\mathrm{depth}(T)}$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a decision tree with real outputs, indexed by an available set of coordinates
$f$ maps the binary cube to $\mathbb Z$
$T$ computes the real-valued function induced by $f$
